title: Chips to Start-ups Programme Strengthens India’s Semiconductor Design Ecosystem and Industry Ready Talent
subtitle: Over 68,000 Students Trained and 254 Chip Designs Successfully Taped Out Under C2S Programme
body_text:
Guided by the vision of the Hon'ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi to make India a global hub for semiconductor chip design, the Government has undertaken focused policy interventions and sustained investments in semiconductor education, research, and design infrastructure, thereby strengthening the country's semiconductor design ecosystem and talent base.
Chips to Start-ups (C2S) Programme has been initiated for capacity-building across the country and to address the issue of workforce talent gap and chip design infrastructure in the semiconductor design area. C2S Programme aims to generate 85,000 numbers of industry-ready manpower at B.Tech, M.Tech, and PhD levels specialized in semiconductor chip design area.
Under the C2S Programme:
i. More than 68,000 students have been trained under the programme so far.
ii. Access to advanced Electronic Design Automation (EDA) tools from Synopsys,   Cadence, Siemens EDA, Ansys, Keysight, Silvaco, Renesas-Altium, AMD-Xilinx, AsterQuanta, Compcarta, Cadre and AMD-Xilinx has been provided to 332 academic institutions across the country.
iii. Participating institutions have successfully taped out 254 chip designs, comprising 175 designs at the 180 nm technology node at SCL, Mohali, and 79 designs at overseas semiconductor foundries.
In the State of Andhra Pradesh:
(i) 23 academic institutions have been provided access to advanced EDA tools under the C2S Programme, with cumulative utilization exceeding 4.34 lakh tool-hours as per list given below:

Siddhartha Engineering College, Vijayawada 11 Anil Neerukonda Institute of Technology & Sciences (ANITS), Visakhapatnam 12 Vishnu Institute of Technology, AP 13 Sagi Rama Krishnam Raju (SRKR) Engineering College, Andhra Pradesh 14 GMR Institute of Technology (GMRIT), Andhra Pradesh 15 G. Pullaiah College of Engineering and Technology, Kurnool 16 Koneru Lakshmaiah Education Foundation, Guntur 17 Vignan's Institute of Information Technology, Visakhapatnam 18 Mohan Babu University, Tirupati, Andhra Pradesh 19 Narayana Engineering College, Gudur, Andhra Pradesh 20 Sri Vasavi Engineering College, Tadepalligudem, Andhra Pradesh 21 Gayatri Vidya Parishad College of Engineering, Visakhapatnam 22 Santhiram Engineering College, Nandyal, Kurnool 23 National Institute of Electronics and Information Technology Tirupati
(ii) The following research projects have been financially supported to promote semiconductor chip design research and strengthen capacity building across four academic institutions:
a) Development of a secure RISC-V processor for cryptographic applications – Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Tirupati.
b) Development of a hardware accelerator to improve computing performance for high-performance computing and cyber-physical systems – Indian Institute of Information Technology Design and Manufacturing (IIITDM) Kurnool.
c) Development of an energy-efficient neuromorphic processor for edge Internet of Things (IoT) applications – National Institute of Technology (NIT) Andhra Pradesh.
d) Development of a memory-efficient co-processing unit for edge Artificial Intelligence (AI) applications – Shri Vishnu Engineering College for Women, Bhimavaram.
The projects are currently at various stages of design and development. Depending on their scope and maturity, they are expected to progress towards prototype validation, including tape-out at semiconductor foundries, wherever applicable.
This information was given by Union Minister of State for Electronics and IT Shri Jitin Prasada in Lok Sabha on 12.08.2026

enrichment.summary: In response to a Lok Sabha question on 12 August 2026, MoS Electronics & IT Jitin Prasada informed Parliament that under the Chips to Start-ups (C2S) Programme, over 68,000 students have been trained against a target of 85,000 industry-ready professionals in semiconductor chip design. The programme has provided 332 academic institutions across India access to advanced Electronic Design Automation (EDA) tools, and participating institutions have successfully taped out 254 chip designs (175 at 180nm node at SCL Mohali, 79 at overseas foundries). Andhra Pradesh alone has 23 institutions with EDA access and four funded research projects on RISC-V processors, hardware accelerators, neuromorphic processors, and AI co-processing units.
enrichment.context:
The Chips to Start-ups (C2S) Programme is a component of India's broader Semiconductor Mission, launched to build a domestic talent pipeline and design ecosystem in VLSI/chip design, complementing the India Semiconductor Mission's fabrication and packaging incentives. It addresses a long-standing gap: India has historically been strong in chip design services (many global semiconductor firms have design centres in India) but lacked a formal capacity-building pipeline linking academic training to actual silicon tape-outs. By providing free/subsidised access to costly commercial EDA tools (from Synopsys, Cadence, Siemens EDA, etc.) to engineering colleges, and enabling actual fabrication runs at SCL Mohali (India's government-owned fab) or overseas foundries, the scheme moves students from theoretical VLSI courses to hands-on, tapeout-validated chip design experience.

This matters in the context of India's push for self-reliance in electronics manufacturing and its ambition to become a major node in the global semiconductor supply chain, especially amid geopolitical shifts (US-China tech tensions, Taiwan's dominance in fabrication) that have prompted countries to diversify chip design and manufacturing bases. Talent availability is often cited as India's core comparative advantage in semiconductors even where fabrication capacity remains nascent, making programmes like C2S central to sustaining that edge.

prelims_questions.question: The 'Chips to Start-ups (C2S)' Programme, aimed at building India's semiconductor design talent, is implemented under which of the following?
options: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship
prelims_questions.explanation: The C2S Programme is run by the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) as part of India's semiconductor design ecosystem-building efforts.

prelims_questions.question: SCL Mohali, mentioned in connection with chip tape-outs under the C2S Programme, refers to which facility?
options: Semi-Conductor Laboratory, a government-owned chip fabrication facility
A private venture capital fund for start-ups
prelims_questions.explanation: Semi-Conductor Laboratory (SCL), Mohali is a government-owned fabrication facility used for tape-outs at the 180nm technology node under the C2S Programme.

mains_questions.question: Discuss the significance of talent development programmes like 'Chips to Start-ups' in strengthening India's position in the global semiconductor value chain. What further steps are needed to translate design capability into fabrication capacity?
mains_questions.gs_paper: GS Paper 3 - Science and Technology / Economy

mains_questions.question: India aims to become a global hub for semiconductor design even as it builds fabrication capacity. Examine the rationale behind this strategy and the challenges India faces in achieving self-reliance across the semiconductor value chain.

study_notes.reason: The release is essentially a factual/statistical Parliament reply on a named scheme (C2S) with concrete figures - targets, tools, tape-outs, and institution counts - offering little independent analytical content beyond generic 'talent gap' framing.

prelims.point: Chips to Start-ups (C2S) Programme aims to train 85,000 industry-ready professionals in semiconductor chip design at B.Tech/M.Tech/PhD levels; over 68,000 trained so far.
prelims.why_important: Scheme name, target figure and implementing focus are classic objective-question material under India's Semiconductor Mission.

prelims.point: C2S Programme has given 332 academic institutions access to Electronic Design Automation (EDA) tools from firms like Synopsys, Cadence, Siemens EDA, AMD-Xilinx.
prelims.why_important: Tests knowledge of scheme implementation mechanism (EDA tool access) as a scheme feature.

prelims.point: 254 chip designs taped out under C2S: 175 at the 180nm node at SCL Mohali (India's government-owned fab) and 79 at overseas foundries.
prelims.why_important: SCL Mohali as India's domestic fab and the specific tape-out numbers/technology node are precise, testable facts.

prelims.point: C2S Programme is a component of India's broader Semiconductor Mission (India Semiconductor Mission), focusing on talent and design ecosystem rather than fabrication/packaging incentives.
prelims.why_important: Distinguishing C2S's design/talent focus from ISM's fabrication/packaging incentive focus is a likely 'distinguish between' question.

mains.point: C2S Programme addresses India's historical strength in chip design services but weak linkage between academic training and actual silicon fabrication experience.
mains.analytical_use: Useful for a question on how India can leverage its design talent advantage for self-reliance in electronics manufacturing.

mains.point: Reliance on SCL Mohali's outdated 180nm node and overseas foundries for tape-outs highlights India's limited indigenous advanced fabrication capacity despite strong design talent.
mains.analytical_use: Supports 'Discuss the challenges in India's semiconductor ecosystem' type questions, contrasting design strength with fabrication weakness.
